title: campus-half landing floor hardcodes `10` instead of deriving from the campus entry like N5's EXPECTED
evidence:
testing.expectf(t, campus_window_spawns >= 10*WINDOW*95/100,
		"the campus half must land: in-window campus spawns %d < %d (10/tick × WINDOW × 0.95)", campus_window_spawns, 10*WINDOW*95/100)
detail: The literal 10 (= campus vol 1 × multiplier 10) is correct today but is NOT derived, while EXPECTED at line 647 derives `stream_entries × surge.multiplier × WINDOW`. A campus-volume or multiplier re-tune would silently mis-pin this floor — the exact drift N5's derivation was added to prevent.
recommended_fix: Derive the campus floor from the catalog: sum `e.volume` over streaming-class entries with `source_role == .Campus`, then × `surge.multiplier` × WINDOW × 95/100, mirroring N5.

title: usage() omits the new `fold-check` verb from the runtime usage message
evidence: fmt.eprintln("usage: harness run|save [demo...] [--stats-out <path>] | replay <demo> <log.bin> | drift-check | preview-check | stats-check <demo> | input-parity [save] | palcheck | map-preview <seed> [out.png]")
detail: `fold-check` is registered at main.odin:142 (`if verb == "fold-check"`) but is absent from the usage() line, so `harness` with no args and `fold-check` arity errors print a help string that never mentions the new subcommand, breaking the harness's list-every-verb convention.
recommended_fix: Append `| fold-check <prev-hash> <prev-tick1>` to the usage() string in harness/main.odin.
